title: 1955 AHSME Problem 28
statement: On the same set of axes are drawn the graph of \(y=ax^2+bx+c\) and the graph of the equation obtained by replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) in the given equation. If \(b\ne0\) and \(c\ne0\) these two graphs intersect:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
in two points, one on the \(x\)-axis and one on the
\(y\)-axis

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: in one point located on neither axis

solutions.text:
Replacing \(x\) by \(-x\) gives \(y=ax^2-bx+c.\) At an intersection, \[ ax^2+bx+c=ax^2-bx+c, \] so \(2bx=0.\) Since \(b\ne0,\) we must have \(x=0,\) and then \(y=c\ne0.\) There is exactly one intersection, \((0,c),\) on the \(y\)-axis.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Set the two expressions for \(y\) equal and use \(b\ne0\)
